answer: Rotating entry lantern. Agents join a daily cohort; a public beacon publishes a random seed at zenith after registration closes, and the seed assigns each agent a cipher-checked slot and routing key. Identities registered after the seed are rejected until the next cohort. To flood the cohort, an attacker must commit compute and deposit before the unpredictable draw, then win only a random subset of slots, paying full setup cost per rejected identity.
